title: Temporal Rollout Inspector and Hybrid-Metric Card: token set and interaction choreography
creator: Rafael Ortega
summary: Create a cohesive token set and interaction choreography for a left-rail Rollout Inspector paired with a new hybrid-density metric card used throughout cost and SLA dashboards.
description: This ticket scopes the design system work required to ship a Rollout Inspector pattern (left-rail micro-surface that binds to a selected deployment/route) and a complementary Hybrid-Metric Card component that adapts density across contexts (compact list, deck, expanded chart). Work includes tokens, component variants, motion specs, accessibility checks, and a shippable Figma file with handoff-ready specs.
goals: Define a minimal, semantically named token subset for adaptive density (spacing, type scale, iconography cadence) that supports compact and expanded metric card variants
Design the Rollout Inspector interaction model with clear canary/cutover states, timeline scrubbing, and fallback affordances for offline data
Prototype microinteractions for rollout state transitions and metric card density toggles to validate perceptual continuity
Produce accessibility-ready specs (keyboard nav, focus states, motion-reduction alternatives) and a Figma library page for engineers
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with dedicated 'Rollout Inspector' and 'Hybrid Metric Card' pages and documented component tokens
Token naming follows semantic convention and includes alt-path tokens for 'compact' and 'dense' layout modes
Interaction prototype validated in 2 design reviews and one accessibility pass with engineering feedback
Handoff includes CSS/token export mapping, a PRD link, and a small implementation checklist for frontend engineers
design_notes: Hybrid-Metric Card supports three density thresholds: compact (list), default (card), expanded (chart + details). Layout breakpoints determined by container width and explicit user toggle.

Rollout Inspector sits as an anchored left rail that can pin to a route; it surfaces active rollout fingerprints, A/B cohort counts, canary latency sparkline, and a timeline scrubber for historical snapshots.
We use semantic tokens for spacing (space-1..space-8) but expose 'space-inline-compact' and 'space-inline-wide' to support the hybrid modes without proliferation.
Motion: use 120ms ease-out for short transitions (state toggles) and 240ms ease-in-out for timeline scrubbing. Provide reduced-motion variants that skip crossfades and use instant reveals.

Color tokens: introduce 'status-rollout-primary' and 'status-rollout-muted' for canary vs baseline states to decouple from existing product status palette. Add contrast-focus token for keyboard outlines.
decisions: Adopt semantic token prefix 'inspector-' for all rollout surface tokens to avoid accidental collisions with dashboard tokens
Use a single Hybrid-Metric Card component with internal variants instead of separate components to simplify analytics instrumentation and QA
Prefer explicit user toggle for density where available; fallback to container-driven responsive collapse when toggle is not present
Prototype timeline scrubber as scrub + snap to nearest snapshot with hover preview, deferring granular scrub performance tuning to runtime telemetry
concerns: Edge-case: very long route names may push layout; plan for name truncation and a hover tooltip with full route id
Engineering: need clear mapping between figma tokens and runtime token names to avoid drift; propose a small automation script to export tokens
Performance: timeline scrubber may create many network queries if naive; recommend bundling snapshots and memoizing preview data at the service layer
